findings.evidence: The Dashboard section (lines 238-281) spends about 45 lines on UI layout: filter-bar order, the two-line clamp, chart types and the 150ms debounce. An agent running the pipeline and reporting results does not act on these details.
findings.fix: Keep only the rules that change what the agent reports (the em dash for an unknown price or date, the conditional badge, the inferred-family rendering, chart dedup). Move the rest of the UI description into a reference file, or delete it.

findings.evidence: "The PRD's own intended trigger is ... not something this phase's own automated delivery performs on the user's behalf."
findings.fix: Replace the PRD and phase narrative with one behavioural line: 'Run classify only when the user asks for it, after real history has been captured.'

findings.evidence: Subcommands are listed with a single `run` example. Nothing helps the agent pick a partial run (capture, refine or dashboard alone) from the user's request.
findings.fix: Add a short decision list: new data wanted -> run; only a UI refresh -> dashboard; inferred families wanted -> classify then dashboard; empty page -> refine then dashboard.

findings.evidence: "Both the `run` and `dashboard` subcommands open the generated file in the default browser automatically ... there is no opt-out flag." The NEVER list does not cover the side effect this causes in headless or SSH sessions.
findings.fix: Add to NEVER: 'Never run `run` or `dashboard` in a headless or CI shell expecting no side effect: both launch the default browser, and there is no opt-out flag.'

findings.evidence: The description is declarative ("Run the local ... pipeline"), has no near-miss boundary against general token-billing or cost questions, and ends on internal jargon ("never a hosted-database Artifact").
findings.fix: Run the local capture-refine-dashboard pipeline over Claude Code, opencode, Codex, Cursor and rtk session logs, and open the static HTML usage-metrics dashboard. Use this skill when the user asks about usage metrics, a usage dashboard, how they use their AI CLIs, which runtime, model or command family they run most, per-session token or price totals from local logs, grep-family counts by session, or a filterable, sortable view of shell commands their coding agents ran, even without naming the dashboard. Not for exporting or sharing data with a hosted service, external billing pages, or explaining what a single shell command does.

findings.evidence: SKILL.md is 324 lines and has no references/. The 29-line schema list, the Dashboard UI detail and the Codex tool-name enumeration load on every run, though only queries or debugging need them.
findings.fix: Move the refined_commands schema, the dashboard UI detail and the Codex tool-name enumeration into references/schema.md and references/dashboard.md. Add gated reads, for example 'Read references/schema.md before writing any SQL against refined.db.'

findings.evidence: The SQL guidance mandates two-branch dedup, but the skill gives an exact query only for a plain row count. Agents must hand-write the dedup SQL, which is the fragile operation.
findings.fix: Add one exact deduplicated token or price SUM query, using (session_id, turn_id) and the (session_id, raw_ref) fallback for null turn_id, to copy verbatim.

findings.evidence: `--help` prints only `usage: ai-kit-usage-metrics.py {capture|refine|dashboard|classify|run}`, with no description, outputs or exit codes. The run summary is not structured output, so the agent needs a separate sqlite one-liner to count rows. The evals and trigger queries (6 evals, 20 queries split 10/10) and tests/test_ai_kit_usage_metrics.py are solid.
findings.fix: Make --help describe each subcommand, its outputs and its exit codes. Have run print a JSON summary to stdout (dashboard path, rows per runtime, failed sources), and add an eval that asserts on it.

findings.evidence: The classify sequence is written as bare `ai-kit-usage-metrics.py classify` / `ai-kit-usage-metrics.py dashboard`. As written it is not runnable, and it breaks from the `python3 "$TOOLS_PY"` form the skill requires elsewhere.

"`refined.db` missing (a `dashboard` run on its own shows an empty page): run `refine` before `dashboard`." The skill does not cover refine itself having nothing to read because no capture ran, or the sqlite count query failing when refined.db does not exist.
findings.fix: State the order explicitly: if raw/*.jsonl is also missing, run capture (or plain run) first. Check that refined.db exists before running the count query, and report zero rows otherwise.
